tasks.short: Record plant growth counts while walking the bay.

steps.what: Look at the plants in this glasshouse bay
Count clusters or height on those plants
Record the growth count for that bay
Retype the growth count into the workbook

tasks.design: She still looks at the plants and still counts. The {OTHER} plant register is that same write: bay, crop, count and stage, taking the same time as the paper line. The retype into the {SPREADSHEET} stops only because those fields are already stored; if she still keeps only paper, the retype and its saving do not apply.
tasks.previous_blocker: The count lived on a paper line in the bay, and a workbook row was a second write of the same figures.
tasks.enabler_now: A register she fills under glass can be the only record, so the workbook row is the same entry rather than a later copy.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to see the plant and count it. The register does not decide what the number means.
tasks.human_edge: She can tell a real cluster from a broken stem, and she chooses the figure that goes on the bay.
tasks.altitude: The week is still in the bay. She still decides what to record, and she gains no say over the crop.

reach.task: Keep the planting record for each bay
reach.learn: The register can open a bay only when that record already has a plot id and a crop id. It does not invent them.

evidence.claim: A greenhouse app registers plants and clusters while the worker is in the greenhouse.

Storing which worker entered each greenhouse count can be monitoring of behaviour or performance and can need works-council consent. This design stores the count on the bay and does not store her name. The digest names the Dutch works-councils act; other countries differ.
Replacing the paper line with one register entry removes a second workbook write of the same count. It does not shorten the look or the count. The share of that second write is not measured here.

assumptions: Focal work is the look, the count, the write of the growth count, and her own later retype into the workbook. The supervisor's planting record is other-role time.
Test the register's own bay form before any custom code. Runtime of that register is not her labour.
s1 and s2 stay at full length. The register does not look at the plant and does not count it.
s3 stays at full length. The phone entry replaces the paper line and takes the same time. It is not a second write on top of paper.

The growth count's fields are bay id, crop id, count, stage and the time she writes them. She produces count, stage and the time in s3, and that time is the whole of s3. Bay id and crop id are produced by the supervisor on the planting record when the crop went in. If that record has no bay id she types the bay name inside s3, still at full length, and no step guesses a bay.

s4 is removed only when s3 is already the stored record, so the workbook row would repeat fields she typed. If the site has no second workbook, s4 does not exist and its saving does not apply. Nothing reads a count she did not type.
unknowns: Whether this site already has a second workbook row for each growth count, or only the paper line.
Whether a planting record already names every bay before she walks it.
research_questions: What share of her recording time is the later workbook retype, as against the look and the count in the bay?

already_counted.description: She still looks, counts and types every growth count.

incremental.description: Retype a count she filed on the wrong bay.
Supervisor keeps plot id, crop id and planting date on each bay so the register can open it. A missing bay id is typed by her inside s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A week of routine counts where she already retypes each figure into a workbook, and the register replaces that retype only. The look, the count and the first write stay at full length. If the workbook row does not exist, the low end is the right end.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Count shed materials and order what is short.

steps.what: Look through stored materials in the shed
Count what is left of each material
Maintain the inventory quantity on the shed sheet
Decide the ordering quantity for each shortage
Ask the supplier to send those materials
Retype those ordering lines into the order sheet

tasks.design: The {OTHER} stock list is the shed sheet: she still looks, still counts and still types every quantity, and she still decides the ordering quantity and phones the supplier. Nothing raises an order from a par level. The retype into the {SPREADSHEET} stops only when the ordering lines she wrote are already the record; a buyer who types the order is outside this task, and that saving does not move.
tasks.previous_blocker: The quantity lived on a shed sheet, and the same lines were typed again into a purchasing sheet before the order went out.
tasks.enabler_now: One stock list can hold the quantity she counted and the ordering lines she decided, so a second sheet is a repeat of fields she already wrote.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to see the shed and judge what the week will use. The supplier still needs her own request.
tasks.human_edge: She knows what this crop week will use, including a substitute the list does not name.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes about who decides the order. She still walks the shed and still asks the supplier.

reach.task: Keep fuel and parts for the machines
reach.learn: This list is pots, ties and substrate. His fuel and parts are a different count and are not filled from these lines.

evidence.claim: A list that already names the material lets her keep one write of the quantity and the ordering lines. No product in the digest keeps a pot, tie or substrate store, and none of them decides an order quantity. The shed walk and the phone call stay.

assumptions: Focal work is the shed walk, the count, the inventory line, the ordering decision, the call to the supplier, and her own retype of those ordering lines. The supplier's reply is not her time. A buyer who places the order is not this task.
Test a stock list in the register already used for the crop before custom code.
s1, s2, s3, s4 and s5 stay at full length. Looking, counting, writing the quantity, deciding how many to order, and asking the supplier are not shortened.

No order is created from a par level. There is no par field in this task. Order quantity is produced by her in s4, at full length. Quantity on hand is produced by her count in s2 and written in s3, at full length. Material name and unit, when the list already has them, were entered by the supervisor when the material was first stocked. A material with no name is written by her inside s3, still at full length.
s6 is removed only when it would retype ordering lines s4 already stored: material name and order quantity. If she never keeps that second sheet, or a buyer types it, s6 is not her saving.
unknowns: Whether she retypes the ordering lines herself, or a buyer types them.
Whether the shed sheet already lists every material name before she counts.
research_questions: Who places the supplier order today, the farmworker or a buyer?

already_counted.description: She still walks the shed, counts, writes quantities, decides the order and phones the supplier.

incremental.description: Add a material the list does not name, and correct a quantity she mis-counted.
Supervisor adds material name and unit when a material is first stocked. That is not a par level and it does not place an order.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A month where she herself retypes ordering lines into a second sheet, and that retype is the only cut. The walk, the count, the decision and the call stay at full length. If a buyer types the order, the low end is the right end.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect plants and bud ties for quality.

steps.what: Inspect plants and bud ties on the row
Assess quality of that tie and that bud
Set aside the plant whose tie fails
Tell the supervisor which row failed inspection

tasks.design: She inspects the plant and the bud tie, decides the quality, sets a failure aside, and tells the supervisor. Nothing scores the tie, and nothing writes a quality code another role could read.
tasks.previous_blocker: The quality of a bud tie is a look at the plant, and no record holds that look.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes the need to see the tie and the bud.
tasks.still_hard: A photo would still need her judgement. The digest has no product that checks a bud tie.
tasks.human_edge: She feels whether the tie holds and sees whether the bud is sound.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still inspects every plant she is given.

reach.learn: A failed bud tie is set aside here and said aloud. There is no quality code for the grader to import.

evidence.claim: Inspecting a bud and a tie is a look and a judgement. No product in the digest assesses that quality, and this design does not add a camera or a score.

assumptions: Focal work is the inspection, the quality judgement, setting the plant aside, and telling the supervisor. No step is shorter.

No quality code is stored. A later role cannot read a pass or fail from a system, because she did not produce one. The producer of the judgement is her look in s2, kept as the set-aside plant and the words she says.
No tool is added, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether a failed plant is only set aside, or also written on a sheet this site keeps.
research_questions: Does the supervisor expect only the set-aside plant and a word, or a written fail as well?

already_counted.description: She still inspects, judges, sets failures aside and tells the supervisor.

incremental.description: No tool is added, so there is no upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The inspection, the judgement, the set-aside and the telling stay at full length. There is no second write to remove.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week stays under glass and in the shed. A plant register does not judge growth or a bud tie, and it does not place an order. She still counts, still decides what to order, and still inspects.
reach: first-line supervisor of farming, fishing, and forestry workers
skills_to_grow: Type the bay name herself when the planting record has no bay id, and do not leave a blank bay.
Write a material the stock list does not name before treating the quantity as complete.
Leave a failed bud tie as her own look, with no quality code for someone else to import.
role.ambitious_version: Every bay she already walks has one growth count on the plant register that day, and the shed list holds the quantities she counted, while the order and the bud-tie judgement stay in her hands.

job.title: Farmworkers and Laborers, Crop, Nursery, and Greenhouse
